features.name: Academic credentials
features.description: This captures the level and strength of the applicant's formal technical academic preparation as presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: This captures experience designing agent-based systems with autonomous behavior plus explicit guardrails, supervision, permissions, or supporting control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No direct agentic-system design described.
Mentions agents, automation, or multi-step workflows only in broad terms.
Clear experience pairing agents with back-end services or constraints.
Sophisticated description of agent autonomy plus guardrails such as permissions, auditing, bounded actions, or explicit control planes.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: This captures whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering problem-solving and system improvements.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production experience
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has shipped AI-enabled systems in production and understands the reliability, evaluation, and failure-mode work required to operate them responsibly.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: This captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers succeed through secure defaults, usable tooling, and reduced friction rather than policing or gatekeeping.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Engineering rigor and maintainability
features.description: This captures whether the applicant emphasizes disciplined, reliable, maintainable engineering with attention to testing, operability, failure modes, and long-term system care.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Evidence specificity and impact
features.description: This captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with specific mechanisms, examples, scope, outcomes, or measurable effects rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter establishes Go as a meaningful production language in the applicant's real backend work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness and cohesion
features.description: This captures the letter's overall voice, flow, and memorability as a coherent piece of writing beyond surface correctness and explicit role targeting.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, list-like, or heavily templated prose.
Is competent and readable, but largely generic in voice.
Has a noticeable hook, framing device, or coherent personal story.
Has a strong, memorable voice that reinforces fit without sacrificing substance.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: This captures evidence of ongoing attacker-minded practice outside ordinary development work, especially through CTFs or similar offensive exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: This captures responsibility for code and users beyond the applicant's employer, from upstream fixes to sustained open-source maintenance or ownership.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Ownership and senior responsibility
features.description: This captures the degree of independent ownership, initiative, and direct delivery responsibility the applicant claims over systems or projects.

levels.descriptor: Mostly aspirational language or support-role contribution.
Shows some hands-on contribution but limited ownership.
Shows clear ownership of tools, systems, or reviews.
Shows repeated architecture, design, or lead responsibility with independent judgment.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: This captures how technically substantial, ambitious, and self-directed the applicant's side projects or independent building work appear.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: This captures whether the applicant is specifically drawn to foundational platform or infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: This captures the amount and breadth of hands-on professional experience building, shipping, maintaining, testing, and operating production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: This captures how convincingly the letter shows Python as a substantial production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned.
Python is mentioned, but only as a general tool or scripting language.
Python is clearly used regularly for services, tooling, or automation.
Python is presented as production-grade work, with specifics such as typed or tested services, shared tooling, or major automation ownership.

features.name: Role-specific motivation and alignment
features.description: This captures how specifically and convincingly the letter explains fit for this exact role and maps the applicant's background, interests, and trajectory to it.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: This captures the depth of hands-on experience reviewing systems for security issues through activities like threat modeling, code review, analysis, and remediation follow-through.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: This captures how well the letter understands the role's core problem as scaling security work through principled automation, triage systems, agents, and high-leverage tooling rather than generic software engineering.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific framing beyond wanting security impact.
Shows general interest in secure defaults or automation, but not a sharp view of the problem.
Clearly frames security tooling as a way to scale review, response, or manual workload.
Frames the problem sharply in terms of scarce expert attention, organization-wide signal handling, variant analysis, or systems-level leverage.

features.name: Security certification strength
features.description: This captures the presence and rigor of formal external security credentials offered as validation of security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering identity
features.description: This captures whether the letter presents the applicant as seriously and authentically oriented toward security engineering through values, commitment, identity, or extracurricular security seriousness beyond ordinary product work.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Security partnership orientation
features.description: This captures readiness to collaborate closely with security specialists or partners, including humility about learning from them.

levels.descriptor: No collaboration signal appears beyond applying for the role.
Cross-functional work is implied, but the posture toward security specialists is not explicit.
The letter explicitly shows enthusiasm for close collaboration with security engineers or learning from specialist teammates.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: This captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: This captures proofreading quality and sentence-level mechanical correctness, including spelling, grammar, and copy-editing care.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Genuinely idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly share a broader recurring construct with the other criteria.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.
